# ruv.sgit.ai

> Memory with history for rUv's agentic stack. **ruv.sgit: a Ruflo hive + sgit vaults + Agent Behaviour Policies.** It is a Ruflo hive (a queen and workers running in parallel; Ruflo is MIT, by rUv / ruvnet) whose shared memory and output is one **ephemeral sgit vault per run**: created when the work starts, a branch per worker, every delivery committed and merged, measured when the run closes (commits, files, bytes, what the server stored, a plaintext probe of the server store, a fresh clone compared file by file), then deleted. The ledger of every run is public. Around it: six proofs of concept of sgit vaults and Agent Behaviour Policies (ABPs) inside Ruflo, RuVector, RVM and MetaHarness; a studio of seven animations; and a ten-minute scripted talk for Agentic Engineering Live (Agentics Foundation London, 15 Oct 2026, 7:00 pm slot). Built 14 to 15 Oct 2026 by Claude Code sessions for Dinis Cruz. Since 21 Oct 2026 (v0.2.0) it is the site that offers **the ruv.sgit service**: agent work done by a Ruflo hive under a written mandate per role, with a vault per job that the client keeps, delivered by named providers through a small marketplace that starts with two founding providers, Dinis Cruz and Mondweep Chakravorty. It speaks to three audiences: **clients** who want the work done, **providers** (consultants and service companies) who want to deliver it, and people who want to **learn**; the **proof** sits behind all three.

This file is the briefing for agents working on this site. Every page has the site version in its nav (see Releases). Every number on the site comes from a recorded run (`evidence/` in the repository); "per its README" means read, not run.

## Start here
- **The story now**: memory and storage first (ruv.sgit, ephemeral vaults, the ledger); behaviour policies second (on a fresh project Ruflo's policy engine runs in its legacy mode, which allowed all 11 actions in our trace (receipt reason legacy-default-allow); in its enforce mode, an ABP compiled into its rules stops 6 of 11, 4 denied and 2 sent to a human, with Ruflo's hash-chained receipts).
- **How materials are made**: each piece of feedback starts a ruv.sgit run. The run's spec (`poc/ruv-sgit/runs/<run>.spec.json`) holds the feedback and one task per worker; workers build in parallel; the host delivers each worker's output onto its own vault branch; the run closes into the ledger and the vault is deleted. To make a change, write a spec and run it (commands below), do not hand-edit the generated pages.
- **What is not claimed**: the vault server for ruv.sgit runs is a local SG/Send server (one process, disk storage) on the machine that ran the hive, so the timings are local; the workers are Claude Code subagents of the session that runs the hive (Ruflo holds the queen, roles, tasks and broadcasts; its `hive-mind work` was not used); POC2's memory roundtrip ran locally and its CI jobs need secrets; Ruflo's policy admin needs an interactive terminal and was not worked around.
- **The service, in one line**: enquire to book, a person replies with dates and a quote; no payment on the site, no automation, matching by hand. The plan, its decisions and what was built are in [Article No. 9: from the talk to the service](https://ruv.sgit.ai/articles/next-phase.md) (v1.0.0, approved and built 21 Oct 2026). Menu: For clients · For providers · How it works · Proof · Learn · Join (`assets/site.js`).

## For clients (runs r5-market and r23-service)
- [Home](https://ruv.sgit.ai/index.html): the service in one line, three doors (For clients, For providers, Learn), the engagement path with prices, the founding providers, the proof (numbers read from `data/vaults.json` at load), the rules in four lines, where it started (the talk), built on rUv's stack
- [For clients](https://ruv.sgit.ai/clients/index.html): the engagement path (a free conversation, a first run, expert time, a four-day pilot, the maintained repository), the four offers and prices (`#offers`), the five project types, the providers, what stays yours (your code, your data, your vault), and sections [for companies](https://ruv.sgit.ai/clients/index.html#companies) and [for internal teams](https://ruv.sgit.ai/clients/index.html#teams)
- Four services, mix and match, none automated end to end yet (a person, the provider, starts, watches and hands over every run): **task runs** on shared infrastructure, £10 / £20 / £50 a run, or £9 / £17 / £40 with your own model key (no internet from the run; materials up to 50 or 100 MB; a behaviour policy per role; the vault handed over as a zip or published), **dedicated compute**, £21 / £23 / £36 per 8-hour block (an EC2 instance per task: a £20 platform fee + twice the EC2 cost, EC2 prices from third-party aggregators, to confirm on AWS's price list; not built yet, and SG Compute is not connected to runs), a **maintained repository** subscription, £149 / £499 / £1,500 a month, and **expert time**, £500 / £1,500 / £5,000. The materials sandbox for customer uploads is not built yet. No payment is taken: orders and enquiries are emailed and a person replies with a quote.
- Anybody who implements this implements sgit vaults and Agent Behaviour Policies (ABPs). Ruflo, RuVector, AgentDB, MetaHarness and RVM are rUv's projects (MIT, by rUv / ruvnet): we build on them; we do not sell or own them.
- Redirects (since v0.2.0; the URLs keep working, and the talk's spoken "ruv.sgit.ai/business" stays for good): [business/index.html](https://ruv.sgit.ai/business/index.html) → For clients · [business/consultants.html](https://ruv.sgit.ai/business/consultants.html) → For providers · [business/companies.html](https://ruv.sgit.ai/business/companies.html) → For clients `#companies` · [business/teams.html](https://ruv.sgit.ai/business/teams.html) → For clients `#teams`
- [The shop](https://ruv.sgit.ai/shop/index.html): a cart with no payment, with an optional preferred provider; checkout opens an email with the order to agent@riskmandate.ai (or copy/download the order as JSON). `?add=<offer id>` adds an item.
- [The business model](https://ruv.sgit.ai/articles/ruv-sgit-business-model.md): the plan, written to be copied
- Data: [data/offers.json](https://ruv.sgit.ai/data/offers.json) (every price, with the cost model and its assumptions; source `poc/ruv-sgit/market/model.py`, `economics.md`; cloud prices to be confirmed on AWS's price list) · [data/maps.json](https://ruv.sgit.ai/data/maps.json) (five Wardley maps: whole, runs, compute, repo, expert; drawn by `assets/maps.js`, `RuvMaps.renderAll('[data-map]')`, `data-map-reading` shows each map's reading)
- Contact for everything: agent@riskmandate.ai

## For providers (run r23-service)
- [For providers](https://ruv.sgit.ai/providers/index.html): for consultants and service companies who want to deliver agentic engagements on ruv.sgit: why join, the founding providers (`#providers`), the rules of engagement in brief, how a provider is matched and delivers, how to join
- Founding providers, one profile page each, rendered from [data/providers.json](https://ruv.sgit.ai/data/providers.json) (approved providers only, consented fields only): [Dinis Cruz](https://ruv.sgit.ai/providers/dinis-cruz.html) · [Mondweep Chakravorty](https://ruv.sgit.ai/providers/mondweep-chakravorty.html). Both list the same four offers at the published list prices and say *enquire to book*. Bios drafted on 21 Oct 2026 from public pages (run r21-bios, every fact sourced in `evidence/r21-provider-bios.md`), for each provider to approve; photos to come.
- [Rules of engagement](https://ruv.sgit.ai/rules/index.html): everything open (our code Apache-2.0, materials CC BY 4.0, rUv's projects MIT); you can do this without us; code from engagements through us is open; the client's code and data are the client's; changes committed back; revenue split equally between the parties after direct costs; whoever has the client bills; custom arrangements in writing; every job leaves evidence; credit where it is due. With worked examples and the licences in one table.
- [How it works](https://ruv.sgit.ai/how-it-works/index.html): the engagement path with prices, who does what, how a provider is matched (by hand, for now), the provider workflow from enquiry to handover (`#workflow`), how every job is delivered as a ruv.sgit run, how changes are committed back
- [Join](https://ruv.sgit.ai/join/index.html): [apply as a provider](https://ruv.sgit.ai/join/index.html#provider) (the waiting list) and [keep me posted](https://ruv.sgit.ai/join/index.html#updates). Both forms build an email to agent@riskmandate.ai in your own email app, with "copy as JSON"; no backend, no payment, and applications never go into this repository.

## Proof
- [Proof](https://ruv.sgit.ai/proof/index.html): the hub: the runs and their vault ledger, the published run vaults, the six proofs of concept, the live app, and the talk with its player, narration and write-ups

### ruv.sgit (the runs, the ledger, the vaults)
- [ruv.sgit](https://ruv.sgit.ai/ruv-sgit/index.html): what it is, one run in six steps, every run from the ledger, how to run it
- [ruv.sgit in motion](https://ruv.sgit.ai/ruv-sgit/motion/index.html): a real run animated from its ledger entry (`?run=<id>`; `?review` for the final frame)
- [The vault ledger](https://ruv.sgit.ai/ruv-sgit/ledger/index.html): stats of every vault: lifecycles, commits, bytes, server-held bytes, plaintext found, clone checks, sgit operation timings
- The definition, animated (run r3-define): [the equation](https://ruv.sgit.ai/ruv-sgit/define/equation/index.html) (on the home page), [the layers](https://ruv.sgit.ai/ruv-sgit/define/layers/index.html) (the talk's ruv.sgit slide), [one action's journey](https://ruv.sgit.ai/ruv-sgit/define/journey/index.html); all `?review` for the final frame
- [One ephemeral vault, a case study](https://ruv.sgit.ai/ruv-sgit/case/index.html): one vault start to finish, beside the newsroom's append-lane measurements (`?run=<id>`; `?review` shows all six steps at once; the default is the newest non-smoke run)
- Data: [data/vaults.json](https://ruv.sgit.ai/data/vaults.json) (the ledger; schema in `poc/ruv-sgit/ledger.schema.md`); per-run records in `evidence/ruv-sgit/<run>.json` (every sgit op and Ruflo call with its milliseconds); run specs in `poc/ruv-sgit/runs/`
- Runner: `poc/ruv-sgit/ruvsgit.py` — `server-start`, `open <run> <spec>`, `deliver <run> <worker> <role> <folder>`, `close <run> <workers.json>`, `delete <run>`, `server-stop`. Needs `npm ci` (ruflo 3.56.10), `pip install sgit-ai==0.21.0 sgraph-ai-app-send "mcp<2"`. Keys and the server token live only in `~/.ruv-sgit` (mode 0600).
- Background: [Agent workflows on ephemeral vaults](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/agent-workflows-on-ephemeral-vaults.md) (newsroom.sgit.ai, the pattern and its swarm measurements); [Self-hosting a vault server for agents](https://sgit.ai/docs/self-host-for-agents.md) (sgit.ai, how the local server is run)

### Published run vaults (sealed)
- Example runs end sealed: `poc/ruv-sgit/ruvsgit.py seal RUN` pushes the run's vault (every branch, its whole history) to the sgraph vault server (https://dev.send.sgraph.ai), publishes its read key (on purpose, irreversible, examples only; see BRIEF.md "Public example vaults"), checks a fresh read-only clone and the vault UI, then destroys the vault key so it can never change. The repository keeps only the reference (server, vault id, read key, viewer URL, clone command) in [data/vaults.json](https://ruv.sgit.ai/data/vaults.json); no vault files. Client runs stay private (`delete`).
- [Published run vaults](https://ruv.sgit.ai/examples/index.html): every published vault, read from data/vaults.json at load, with an "Open in the vault UI" button, the clone command and the vault UI embedded read-only (sgit.ai's embed protocol)
- example-01-hello-v2: [open in the vault UI](https://dev.vault.sgraph.ai/en-gb/#sgit_public_read_64e6cbc4b71549d83beb23b2532fe192ed8ec4a66a407cce56e8724e2cccc799:q4hynr3y) · `sgit clone sgit_public_read_64e6cbc4b71549d83beb23b2532fe192ed8ec4a66a407cce56e8724e2cccc799:q4hynr3y` (sealed 2026-10-17, 3 files)
- example-07-meta: [open in the vault UI](https://dev.vault.sgraph.ai/en-gb/#sgit_public_read_a8055b9646bba6e6c8d00b623cb85242842569720c28e87746d42c8bee7e368e:nxmykn2w) · `sgit clone sgit_public_read_a8055b9646bba6e6c8d00b623cb85242842569720c28e87746d42c8bee7e368e:nxmykn2w` (sealed 2026-10-17, 10 files)
- Superseded: example-01-hello → example-01-hello-v2; r14-examples → example-07-meta (first sealed as static folders in this repository, now removed; their vault keys were destroyed, so they were republished as new runs)
- The brief: [Getting started with ruv.sgit](https://ruv.sgit.ai/articles/getting-started.md) (draft: the example ladder, the seal-and-publish lifecycle, the example page format)

### The talk, 15 October 2026
- [The talk](https://ruv.sgit.ai/talk/index.html): the player embedded in the page, the script as swipeable cards, the evening (agenda, the 7:00 pm slot, who is in the room), the run of show, sources for every number, questions to expect, rehearsals
- [Article No. 11: the talk, narrated](https://ruv.sgit.ai/articles/the-talk-narrated.html): how the narrated talk was made (runs r16 to r19), its layouts and features, and how the browser's own voice (Web Speech API) reads it: where voices come from, local or online, why it cannot be saved from the page, why Playwright cannot record it, and why publishing a recorded system voice needs a licence that allows it
- [The talk, narrated](https://ruv.sgit.ai/talk/narration.html): the deck with a timed text narration under it, for a CEO, a CTO and a developer (narration/ceo.json, cto.json, dev.json); each paragraph with the notes it was written from; the script as Markdown and captions as WebVTT
- [Player](https://ruv.sgit.ai/talk/player.html?talk=talk-10.json): plays a timeline on a clock. Keys: Space play/pause; → ← next/previous step (or tap the slide); PageDown/PageUp ↓ ↑ next/previous slide (or swipe); S speed (0.75× to 2×); H auto-advance (off by default: each slide stops at its end); Z the talk timer (wall clock, unaffected by navigation, coloured against the plan); G go to any slide or step; P speaker notes; A audience window (synced); V review (every slide finished, no animation; also `?review`); T next theme; B black; R rehearsal log; X leave; F fullscreen; ? help. A step track and a countdown to the next slide sit under the timeline. Embedded (`&embed`), ⤢ opens it in its own window. Live slides load `assets/clock.js` (a virtual clock: the player pauses, speeds, steps and seeks them; `?once` plays a looping page once; `?ruvt=` starts it part-way; `window.RUV_STEPS` names its steps). `sw.js` keeps every file the talk used (stale-while-revalidate), and the player loads each live slide once in the background.
- Slides made for the talk (run r6-talk): `talk/slides/{claim,stack,ruvector,sgit,abp,history,ledger,services,shop,visit}/index.html` (claim and stack from run r7-claim; sgit and abp from run r8-explain), each a page that plays once and holds, with `?review` for its final frame
- Timelines: [talk-10.json](https://ruv.sgit.ai/talk/talk-10.json) (600 s), [talk-5.json](https://ruv.sgit.ai/talk/talk-5.json) (300 s). A beat: `id, at, dur, title, say, cue?, steps?, slide{layout, speed?, ...}` (speed: the live page runs that much faster, to fit a shorter beat); `extras` (untimed beats after the talk); layouts `title, statement, terminal, table (rows_from: report | abp:<role>), bullets, quote, image, iframe (src, fallback image, type), video`. Beats must tile the talk (each `at` = previous `at` + `dur`); `site/build/validate.py` fails otherwise. Every slide shares one frame: brand strip, title top left, a source line.
- Offline single files: [offline-10.html](https://ruv.sgit.ai/talk/offline-10.html), [offline-5.html](https://ruv.sgit.ai/talk/offline-5.html) (built by `site/build/talk_offline.py`; live pages fall back to screenshots)

## Look and feel
- Five themes from newsroom.sgit.ai (Newsprint, Night, Paper, Blueprint, Ember) in `assets/themes.css` (token blocks copied unchanged), applied before paint by `assets/theme.js` (localStorage `ruv.theme`, or `?theme=` for one page). Every colour on the site is a token; terminal blocks stay dark in every theme. The player, the live app and the ruv.sgit pages read the same tokens.
- Navigation: six groups (For clients, For providers, How it works, Proof, Learn, Join) built by `assets/site.js` since v0.2.0 (until then: Tonight, The idea, Proofs, Articles, Work with us); the footer links For clients and "join as a provider"; the collaboration is written "rUv + sgit".

## Releases
- [Release history](https://ruv.sgit.ai/admin/versions.md) ([versions.json](https://ruv.sgit.ai/admin/versions.json)): the site version is in the nav of every page and increments on every push to `dev`; add a release at the top of `site/admin/versions.json` and run `site/build/versions.py`

## Build and checks
- Run the website locally: `./run-website-locally.sh [port]` at the repo root (Python 3 only, no network; serves site/ on :8080 and opens the talk)
- Offline on a laptop: `bash scripts/offline.sh setup` once (online), then `bash scripts/offline.sh all` with no network: doctor, the POCs, sync and validate, one ruv.sgit run on a local vault server (ledger in `out/offline/`, not the public one), then the site on http://localhost:8080. Third-party scripts are in `site/vendor/` (mermaid 11.12.0, three.js r128, marked 15.0.7; MIT).
- `bash site/build/sync.sh` (POC outputs into the site; then talk_offline.py, articles.py, studio_run.py, versions.py) · `python3 site/build/validate.py` (links, chrome, canonical URLs, secret-shaped strings, the version, timelines that tile) · `npm run site:serve` (http://localhost:8080)
- CI: `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` (GitHub Pages) and `pocs.yml` (POCs; vault jobs need `SGIT_TOKEN`, `SGIT_VAULT_KEY_*`)

## Rules for agents working here
- Never print, log or commit a vault key or token; `git diff` before every commit. Only the public POC vault's read key is published, on purpose.
- Every number on a page comes from a run recorded in `evidence/`; if a tool differs from its docs, trust its `--help` and write it in `evidence/notes.md`.
- Do not weaken a security control to make a demo work (Ruflo's interactive policy admin, its policy-anchor tamper check).
- Attribute rUv's projects correctly (MIT, by rUv / ruvnet). This site's code: Apache-2.0.
